title: Grateful Dead Live at Crystal Ballroom on 1968-02-02
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard tape of a jazzy, raw‑power 1968 show, highlighted by a monster Viola Lee Blues and the soaring “Clementine.”
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller transfer delivers an exceptionally crisp, balanced soundboard recording that lets every instrument shine. Musically the performance is often called a “jazzy masterpiece,” with standout moments on Viola Lee Blues, Clementine, The Other One suite and Dark Star, delivering primal energy and soaring guitar work. Minor quirks such as the truncated Schoolgirl cut are noted, but overall the show is praised as one of the band’s finest early‑year performances.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 5) and enthusiastic comments on both performance and recording; only a few mixed/low scores, so overall rating is very strong.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with excellent balance; Charlie Miller transfer praised as “impeccable.” Minor issue: Good Morning Little School Girl cuts off early.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Described as a jazzy, almost Coltranesque suite; raw, primal energy throughout with tight transitions and soaring improvisations.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s wailing lead guitar and insane licks on Viola Lee Blues receive high praise; his tone is called perfect and gives goose‑bumps.
